jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
flags: UK-001: evidenced amount exceeds the promised amount (different bases; see the contributing rows)

rows.title: Exascale supercomputer and AI Research Resource
rows.promised: Invest in the region of £900 million to build an exascale supercomputer and set up an AI Research Resource.
rows.period: initial investments from 2023; end date not stated
rows.notes: Umbrella for the Edinburgh exascale system (UK-003) and the AI Research Resource (UK-004). Subject to business case process.

delivery.evidence_type: facility operating
delivery.summary: Isambard-AI in Bristol is operating as part of the AI Research Resource, while the Edinburgh national supercomputer is funded but not yet operating.
delivery.notes: Components are assessed in UK-003, UK-004 and UK-005. No single amount is recorded because the component figures in the sources overlap with the roughly £900 million.

rows.title: Foundation Model Taskforce (later Frontier AI Taskforce)
rows.promised: Provide £100 million of start-up funding for a taskforce on safe and reliable foundation models.
rows.notes: Announced as additional to UK-001. Renamed Frontier AI Taskforce in 2023; AI Safety Institute followed.

rows.title: Exascale computer at the University of Edinburgh
rows.promised: Build a national exascale supercomputer at the University of Edinburgh.
rows.amount_as_stated: no amount stated (described as part of the £900 million)
rows.notes: Official page gives no Edinburgh-specific amount. Press (Computer Weekly, UKTN, TechRepublic) later reported £800 million; not used as the amount here.
rows.not_counted_reason: part of UK-001; no amount stated

delivery.evidence_type: audit report
delivery.summary: The Department for Science, Innovation and Technology has allocated £750 million to build the Edinburgh national supercomputer and run it for five years; the National Audit Office reports it is not yet operating and expects a gap after ARCHER2 closes.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: departmental allocation including contingency, as reported by the National Audit Office
delivery.notes: Evidence for the Edinburgh system is held here once; UK-012 is its re-announcement. The Compute Roadmap says the system is expected online in early 2027, which is a plan, not delivery.

rows.title: AI Research Resource, first phase
rows.promised: Launch the first phase of a national AI Research Resource (Isambard-AI in Bristol, Dawn in Cambridge).
rows.notes: Relationship to the £900 million umbrella is disputed in sources (one reports AIRR 'tripled from £100m to £300m'); see gaps.md. Not added to totals.

delivery.evidence_type: facility operating
delivery.summary: The first phase of the AI Research Resource is running: Isambard-AI launched in July 2025 and Dawn in Cambridge is part of the resource.
delivery.notes: The £300 million total is not evidenced. The £225 million for Isambard-AI is recorded under UK-005. Accounts of how this £300 million relates to the £900 million in UK-001 differ (see gaps.md).

rows.title: Isambard-AI supercomputer, Bristol
rows.promised: Fund the Isambard-AI supercomputer at the University of Bristol.

delivery.evidence_type: facility operating
delivery.summary: Isambard-AI launched in Bristol in July 2025 with 5,448 NVIDIA superchips and is allocating compute to researchers and companies.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: investment figure stated by the University of Bristol, the host institution; not a ledger line

rows.title: AI in life sciences and healthcare mission
rows.promised: Fund a £100 million mission to accelerate AI in life sciences and healthcare.

rows.title: Further AI Research Resource funding (Autumn Statement 2023)
rows.promised: Add £500 million of further funding for the AI Research Resource.
rows.notes: Press-reported only; primary Autumn Statement text not retrieved. Reported as shelved in August 2024. See gaps.md.

rows.title: TechFirst skills programme
rows.promised: Invest £187 million in tech and AI skills across schools, graduates, experts and local businesses.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The government's one-year report describes £187 million as committed to TechFirst; the report distinguishes committed money from spent money and no spend figure was read.

rows.title: Industry partnership to train 7.5 million workers in AI skills
rows.promised: Partner with industry so that 7.5 million UK workers gain essential AI skills by 2030.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The one-year report states that over one million free AI courses have been delivered; the count is of courses, not of people trained, so it cannot be compared with the target of 7.5 million workers.
delivery.notes: No amount is stated for this commitment.

rows.title: Twenty-fold expansion of the AI Research Resource
rows.promised: Provide over £1 billion to expand AI Research Resource compute twenty-fold by 2030.
rows.notes: Announced by the Prime Minister at London Tech Week; amount as restated in the Compute Roadmap (17 Jul 2025).

rows.title: Compute Roadmap: up to £2 billion of public compute to 2030
rows.promised: Invest up to £2 billion in public compute infrastructure between 2025 and 2030.
rows.notes: Roadmap states its £1bn, £750m and milestone figures overlap and must not be added.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The one-year report states that £2 billion was committed to expand UK compute twentyfold by 2030; the AI Research Resource has launched with a first phase, and no spend figure or contract awards for the later tranches were read.
delivery.notes: The Compute Roadmap was first published in July 2025 and last updated on 23 April 2026.

rows.title: National supercomputer at the University of Edinburgh (restored)
rows.promised: Provide up to £750 million for a new national supercomputer at the University of Edinburgh.
rows.notes: Revives the Edinburgh exascale project shelved in August 2024. Treated as a re-announcement of UK-003 (judgement call; see README).

delivery.evidence_type: audit report
delivery.summary: Re-announcement of the Edinburgh supercomputer first announced in 2023; delivery evidence is recorded once, under UK-003.

rows.title: Sovereign AI Unit
rows.promised: Back UK AI companies through a Sovereign AI Unit funded with up to £500 million.
rows.notes: Unit first announced in the AI Opportunities Action Plan; the £500m figure is tied to the Spending Review in the Roadmap.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The Sovereign AI Unit has provided £8 million of seed funding to the OpenBind structural dataset consortium; the £500 million is a ceiling, and no investment total was found.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: seed funding stated in the government's one-year report

rows.title: AI Security Institute Alignment Project
rows.promised: Fund the Alignment Project for AI alignment research with £15 million.
rows.notes: Year-level date only on the cited page.

rows.title: AI Security Institute Systemic Safety Grants
rows.promised: Fund Systemic Safety Grants of £8 million.

rows.title: Dawn supercomputer upgrade, Cambridge
rows.promised: Invest £36 million to expand Dawn's AI capacity sixfold (£16m DSIT, £20m UKRI).

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The government confirmed in January 2026 that it will procure a sixfold capacity increase for Dawn in Cambridge by spring 2026; completion was not evidenced.

rows.title: AI Security Institute additional funding
rows.promised: Provide an additional £120 million to the AI Security Institute.

delivery.evidence_type: parliamentary answer
delivery.summary: A written parliamentary answer of 12 October 2026 states that the AI Security Institute has been allocated £240 million over the Spending Review period to 2029-30, with 243 staff; this is an allocation, not spending.
delivery.notes: Whether this allocation includes the additional £120 million in the commitment is not established by the answer, so no amount is recorded against that claim.

rows.title: National AI Biosecurity Initiative
rows.promised: Fund a £165 million initiative including an AI Biosecurity Lab and biosurveillance.

rows.title: AI Biosecurity Lab
rows.promised: Establish an AI Biosecurity Lab with £100 million of government funding.

rows.title: AI Biosecurity Lab: OpenAI and Anthropic commitments
rows.promised: OpenAI to provide £100m in compute and credits and Anthropic up to £100m in credits and support to the AI Biosecurity Lab.
rows.notes: Value stated by government; funded by the companies, so not counted as government spending.
rows.not_counted_reason: part of UK-019; funded by a company

rows.title: National Cyber Shield
rows.promised: Fund a £60 million National Cyber Shield using agentic AI for cyber defence.

rows.title: National Exposure and Real-Time Vulnerability (NERV) Centre
rows.promised: Fund a £70 million centre using AI to find cyber vulnerabilities in critical infrastructure.

rows.title: Sovereign AI Fund top-up
rows.promised: Add £60 million to the Sovereign AI Fund with a physical and industrial AI focus.

rows.title: Sovereign AI R&D Procurement Scheme
rows.promised: Add £60 million for an AI R&D procurement scheme in health, care and AI security.

rows.title: UK Advanced Chip Design Academy
rows.promised: Fund a £18 million chip design academy.

rows.title: AI Challenge Prize
rows.promised: Fund a £15 million AI challenge prize, first award in health.

rows.title: AI Economics Institute
rows.promised: Fund an AI Economics Institute with £23 million over three years.

rows.title: Local AI partnerships with Mayoral Strategic Authorities
rows.promised: Provide £30 million for local AI partnerships.

rows.title: Work on how AI will reshape jobs and industry
rows.promised: Fund £10 million per year of work on how AI will reshape jobs and industry.

rows.title: Manchester Prize for AI research
rows.promised: Award a £1 million prize every year for ten years for progress in critical areas of AI.
rows.notes: Total of £10 million is 10 x the stated annual £1 million (derived, not separately stated).

rows.title: InvestAI initiative
rows.promised: Mobilise €200 billion of investment in AI in Europe.
rows.notes: A target to mobilise public and private capital, not a stated public commitment. Commission funding comes from existing programmes (Digital Europe, Horizon Europe, InvestEU). Excluded from the promised total.

rows.title: InvestAI fund for AI gigafactories
rows.promised: Mobilise €20 billion through a new European fund to finance AI gigafactories.
rows.notes: Press release says four gigafactories; the April 2025 AI Continent Action Plan says up to five; the July 2026 call says up to seven.
rows.not_counted_reason: part of EU-001; mobilisation target (public and private money)

rows.title: First seven EuroHPC AI Factories
rows.promised: Set up seven AI Factories with €1.5 billion of combined national and EU funding.

delivery.evidence_type: grant or contract award
delivery.summary: The first AI Factories have offered services since April 2025 on existing systems; contracts for new systems were signed in March 2026 (Germany) and April 2026 (Sweden, Italy).
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: sum of two total budgets stated in signed-contract releases: €290 million (IT4LIA, Italy) and €29.76 million (Mimer, Sweden); each is 50% EuroHPC and 50% national; covers two of the seven factories
delivery.notes: The €1.5 billion headline is not evidenced in full. HammerHAI's system delivery was planned for the second quarter of 2026 and operation for the second half of 2026; no operating date was found.

rows.title: Second wave of six AI Factories
rows.promised: Set up six more AI Factories with around €485 million of national and EU investment.
rows.notes: Selection date of 12 March 2025 taken from Commission press release IP/25/1013.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: EuroHPC selected six additional AI Factory sites on 12 March 2025 (Austria, Bulgaria, France, Germany, Poland, Slovenia) and lists 19 AI Factories; no contract values for this wave were read.

rows.title: Third wave of six AI Factories
rows.promised: Set up six more AI Factories with over €500 million of joint EU and Member State investment.
rows.notes: Amount is a floor ('over'). Exact day not shown on the page retrieved.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: EuroHPC lists 19 AI Factories and 13 antennas as being implemented; for the Netherlands, one of the later sites, the Dutch government reports that the EU subsidy was awarded in October 2025. Contracts and values for the other sites in this wave were not checked.
delivery.notes: Which sites belong to this wave was not checked site by site.

rows.title: Thirteen AI Factory Antennas
rows.promised: Fund 13 AI Factory Antennas with around €55 million from the EU, matched by participating states.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: EuroHPC selected 13 AI Factory Antennas on 13 October 2025 with about €55 million of EU funding, and the Commission's April 2026 progress release says the antennas are providing regional access; no contract or grant-agreement values were read.
delivery.notes: The selection page describes the antennas as newly selected, with a memorandum of understanding with their linked AI Factories due by mid-2026. The statement that access is being provided is the Commission's own and was not confirmed against an operating service.

rows.title: AI Factories and Antennas: over €2.6 billion committed
rows.promised: Total of over €2.6 billion committed by the EU and participating countries to AI Factories and Antennas.
rows.notes: Aggregate of EU-003 to EU-006; not added again.

rows.title: '€10 billion' AI Factories support (as first described)
rows.promised: Existing support for AI Factories of €10 billion, co-financed by the EU and Member States.
rows.notes: Later Commission pages describe €10 billion as total EuroHPC supercomputing plus AI Factories investment for 2021-2027, so it is not an AI-only figure. See gaps.md.
rows.not_counted_reason: total supercomputing and AI Factories budget, not an AI-only line

rows.title: AI Gigafactories call for tenders
rows.promised: Support up to seven AI Gigafactories with up to €10 billion of EU and national funding, expected to unlock at least €20 billion of private investment.
rows.period: two phases; bulk from the 2028-2035 budget framework
rows.notes: Call page says only part is covered by the current budget framework and 'the bulk' comes from the next MFF (2028-2035), which is not yet adopted. Implements EU-002; the EU share is up to €100m + €400m per project (lot 1, four projects) and €200m + €800m (lot 2, three projects).

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The call opened on 30 July 2026 with a submission deadline of 12 November 2026; selection is expected in early 2027 and no gigafactory exists yet.

rows.title: Apply AI Strategy
rows.promised: Mobilise around €1 billion from existing EU funding programmes to speed AI adoption in key sectors.
rows.notes: Drawn from existing programmes, so partly overlaps with other lines.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The Commission's April 2026 progress release says €1 billion in Apply AI funding calls is earmarked; calls seen include Horizon Europe digital calls of €221.8 million and €85.5 million (January 2026) and Digital Europe calls of €63.2 million (April 2026). No grant awards were read, and one pilot call (€9 million, 19 proposals) reports results for February 2027.
delivery.notes: Earmarked calls are not awards, so no amount is recorded. The frontier AI grand challenge selected its leading project in June 2026 according to the Commission's research page. The call amounts overlap with other EU rows and are not summed.

rows.title: AI in Science Strategy: compute for researchers
rows.promised: Provide €600 million from Horizon Europe to expand compute access for science, including access to AI Gigafactories.
rows.notes: Republication of the Commission press release. Possible overlap with EU-012 not resolved; see gaps.md.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The 2026-2027 Horizon Europe work programme sets up an AI in Science call of about €90 million, and a RAISE pilot call closed on 21 April 2026; no award results were found, and the €600 million figure for compute is not matched to a budget line.
delivery.notes: Sources give the AI in Science call as €90 million (Commission news item, January 2026) and a RAISE package of €100 million (work programme annex); the work programme also states at least €867 million for AI in science elsewhere in the programme. These are not reconciled with the €600 million.

rows.title: RAISE pilot (Resource for AI Science in Europe)
rows.promised: Fund the RAISE pilot with €107 million under Horizon Europe.
rows.notes: The strategy document COM(2025) 724 says €108 million; the launch press release says €107 million. See gaps.md.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The Commission launched the RAISE pilot on 3 November 2025 with €107 million under Horizon Europe; the first pilot calls closed on 21 April 2026 and no award results were found.
delivery.notes: The launch page mentions no calls or awards. Topic budgets seen in the work programme are €15.0 million and €12.8 million (networks of excellence) and €17 million (Science for AI pilot); these are call budgets, not awards.

rows.title: Alice Recoque exascale supercomputer (France)
rows.promised: Procure a second European exascale supercomputer, hosted in France, with a total acquisition budget of €354.8 million, half from the EU and half from France, the Netherlands and Greece.
rows.notes: Filed under the EU because EuroHPC owns the system; the French, Dutch and Greek shares are not separated in the source, so they are not repeated in the national ledgers. Other figures for the same system differ: the June 2024 hosting-agreement release says total cost of ownership above €544 million, and the November 2025 releases say €554 million over five years of operation. See gaps.md. Hosting agreement signed 18 June 2024; contract with Eviden announced 18 November 2025.

delivery.evidence_type: grant or contract award
delivery.summary: EuroHPC and the host consortium signed the supply contract with Eviden, announced on 18 November 2025; installation began in 2026 and GENCI expects commissioning in 2027.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: total budget for acquisition stated in the contract-signing release (EuroHPC 50%)
delivery.notes: This is a budget, not the contract price, which the release does not state.

rows.title: Commission and EIB Group memorandum on financing AI gigafactories
rows.promised: Cooperate on EIB Group financing for AI gigafactories alongside the InvestAI fund.
rows.notes: Memorandum of understanding. The source states no amount.
rows.not_counted_reason: part of EU-002; no amount stated

rows.title: IA-Cluster call for research and training hubs
rows.promised: Fund 5 to 10 world-class AI research and training hubs with €500 million from France 2030.
rows.notes: Announced at VivaTech 2023. Nine winners and €360 million awarded on 21 May 2024 (see delivery.json, not repeated here).

delivery.evidence_type: grant or contract award
delivery.summary: A press release of 22 May 2024 names nine winning AI Clusters sharing €360 million from France 2030, against the €500 million originally called.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: award total stated by the government for the nine winners
delivery.notes: The sources read do not say whether the other €140 million was awarded elsewhere or left unawarded. They also do not say whether the clusters are installed.

rows.title: Call for projects: digital commons for generative AI
rows.promised: Fund shared datasets and test bases for generative AI through a €40 million call for projects run by Bpifrance.

delivery.evidence_type: grant or contract award
delivery.summary: Seven new winners of the generative AI digital commons call were announced in May 2024; the sources read give no award amount.
delivery.notes: The original call amount of €40 million is not matched to awards.

rows.title: Jean Zay supercomputer power increase
rows.promised: Increase the computing power of the Jean Zay supercomputer and open it more widely to AI development.
rows.notes: The press release gives no amount. GENCI's 2024 annual report says the Jean Zay extension was financed by France 2030 in response to a presidential announcement of 'May 2023', which differs from the 16 June 2023 date of the press release. See gaps.md.

delivery.evidence_type: facility operating
delivery.summary: GENCI reports that Jean Zay's computing power was quadrupled and the Jean Zay 4 extension inaugurated in May 2025.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: investment of about €40 million stated in GENCI's 2024 annual report for the 2024 Jean Zay extension, funded by France 2030; assumed to be the same extension (moderate confidence)

rows.title: Call for projects: accelerating generative AI use in the economy
rows.promised: Open a France 2030 call for projects, run by Bpifrance, for consortia of generative AI developers and users.
rows.notes: The release states no amount for the call.

rows.title: National AI strategy: nearly €2.5 billion from France 2030
rows.promised: Dedicate nearly €2.5 billion of France 2030 to AI under the national AI strategy.
rows.notes: Cumulative envelope that includes the 2018 to 2022 first phase (about €1.5 billion) and amounts already announced in FR-001 and FR-002. The sources do not split it into new and earlier money, so it is listed but not added to the promised total. Official pages disagree on phase 2: €1 billion (entreprises.gouv.fr) and €1.5 billion (presse.economie.gouv.fr, 4 April 2024). See gaps.md.
rows.not_counted_reason: cumulative envelope that overlaps FR-001, FR-002 and earlier years

rows.title: AI Action Summit: €109 billion of investment in AI in France
rows.promised: Announce an investment of €109 billion in AI in France.
rows.notes: The source states the headline figure without a public and private split. Treated as a mobilisation figure and kept out of the promised total until a breakdown of the public share is found. See gaps.md.

rows.body: Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF)
rows.title: BMBF AI Action Plan
rows.promised: Invest over €1.6 billion in AI in the legislative period through the BMBF AI Action Plan, almost €500 million of it in 2024.
rows.notes: Presented on 23 August 2023; the full plan was published on 7 November 2023. The BMFTR AI pages (successor ministry) repeat the same sentence for 'the current legislative period' without a date; see gaps.md.

delivery.evidence_type: budget line
delivery.summary: The ministry's own summary shows AI budget lines of €427.2 million for 2023 and €483.3 million for 2024 (planned figures); outturn for those years and budget lines for 2025 and 2026 were not found.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: sum of planned budget lines for 2023 and 2024, not outturn
delivery.notes: The sum is arithmetic on two stated figures. It is a budget, not spending.

rows.title: Hightech Agenda Deutschland (AI as one of six key technologies)
rows.promised: Adopt a research and technology agenda that names AI as one of six key technologies, with flagship initiatives for each.
rows.notes: The Federal Research Ministry later states at least €18 billion for the whole agenda across all six technologies. No AI share is given, so no amount is recorded here.

rows.body: Federal Ministry for Digital Affairs and State Modernisation (BMDS)
rows.title: National Data Centre Strategy
rows.promised: Double data centre capacity in Germany and at least quadruple AI and high-performance computing capacity by 2030, through 28 measures.
rows.notes: Cabinet decision date of 18 March 2026 taken from the Federal Government FAQ. The strategy document is dated March 2026 and states targets, not amounts.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The digital ministry reports that 25 of the 28 measures had started and four were completed six months after the strategy was adopted.
delivery.notes: Self-reported by the ministry responsible for the strategy. No independent check found.

rows.body: Federal Ministry for Digital Affairs and State Modernisation (BMDS)
rows.title: Support for at least one AI gigafactory in Germany
rows.promised: Support the build and operation of at least one AI gigafactory in Germany as a public-private partnership with EuroHPC and the Commission.
rows.notes: Measure 1 of the strategy. The document describes the gigafactory as a primarily commercial project and states no federal amount. The EU call opened at the end of July 2026 (see EU-009).
rows.not_counted_reason: part of DE-003; no amount stated

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The research ministry states that the EU competition for gigafactory sites opened on 30 July 2026; no German consortium has been selected.

rows.title: New AI compute capacity for National High Performance Computing
rows.promised: Provide €30.7 million to 2030 for new AI compute capacity in the National High Performance Computing network.
rows.notes: Date is that of the press release, the first dated source found; the page does not give a decision date or the budget line.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The digital ministry's September 2026 release says €30.7 million flows until 2030 into new AI computing capacity for national high-performance computing; no grant award, contract or operating system was found.
delivery.notes: The release restates the commitment. No amount is recorded as evidenced because restating the figure is not evidence of delivery. Not searched: the federal budget plan and Bundestag documents.

rows.title: IPCEI projects in cloud, AI and data infrastructure
rows.promised: Make around €3 billion available for European flagship projects (IPCEI) in cloud, AI and data infrastructure.
rows.notes: The figure covers cloud, AI and data infrastructure together with no AI split, so it fails the AI-line test and is not added to the promised total. Date is that of the press release; the page gives no first-announcement date. A 2021 federal report also mentions up to €3 billion for two IPCEI, so the money may predate this statement. See gaps.md.
rows.not_counted_reason: cloud, AI and data infrastructure with no AI split

rows.body: CDP Venture Capital (state-controlled investor), with the Ministry of Enterprises and Made in Italy
rows.title: CDP Venture Capital: €1 billion for AI
rows.promised: Dedicate €1 billion of CDP Venture Capital resources to AI: €120 million for technology transfer, €580 million for startups and €300 million for mature companies.
rows.notes: CDP Venture Capital is a state-controlled investment company, so the source tier is 'institution', not a ministry. The Prime Minister thanked CDP for the €1 billion in an undated video message (governo.it page could not be loaded; see gaps.md). A later CDP release describes the same €1 billion as a €500 million AI fund plus €500 million of co-investments, a different split.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: CDP Venture Capital reports more than €300 million of the AI envelope already allocated, supporting about 150 startups and about 20 funds.
delivery.amount_evidenced_basis: lower bound stated by CDP Venture Capital (over €300 million); self-reported by the investor
delivery.notes: A Council of Ministers communiqué seen only as a search snippet gives €313 million in its annexes; the page could not be loaded to confirm.

rows.title: CDP Venture Capital and OpenAI memorandum of understanding
rows.promised: Cooperate on AI startup investment, mentoring and university training programmes through CDP Venture Capital's Artificial Intelligence Fund.
rows.notes: The memorandum states no value of its own; the €1 billion belongs to IT-001.
rows.not_counted_reason: part of IT-001; no amount stated

rows.title: AI law authorises up to €1 billion of AI investment
rows.promised: Authorise up to €1 billion of equity and quasi-equity investment in AI, cybersecurity and enabling technologies through the venture capital support fund and CDP Venture Capital.
rows.notes: Legislative authorisation of the same €1 billion. The source does not say whether it is new money; a later Council of Ministers communiqué describes it as a share of the venture capital support fund's resources. Final Senate vote on 17 September 2025 is inferred from the word 'yesterday' in an article dated 18 September 2025.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: The law authorising up to €1 billion in equity and quasi-equity investments through CDP Venture Capital restates the envelope in IT-001; evidence is recorded once, under IT-001.

rows.body: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy (EZK) via RVO
rows.title: GPT-NL open Dutch language model
rows.promised: Contribute €13.5 million from the first Applied Research Facilities funding round to develop GPT-NL, an open Dutch language model.
rows.notes: Amount from the Cabinet's January 2024 vision. The date of 2 November 2023 is from the Digital Economy Strategy progress report of March 2025.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: SURF reported on 26 February 2026 that the language model is fully trained and that ten launching customers get early access in the first quarter, with a wider rollout in the autumn.
delivery.notes: The page does not state a budget, so no amount is recorded. The page does not state the year of the autumn rollout (context points to 2026).

rows.title: AiNed programme: €204.5 million for AI knowledge, innovation and application
rows.promised: Make €204.5 million available through the AiNed programme of the National Growth Fund for AI knowledge, innovation and use.
rows.notes: Restated by the Cabinet on 18 January 2024. The funds were awarded in earlier Growth Fund rounds (€160.5 million awarded plus €44 million conditionally, per a parliamentary reply), before the period of this ledger, so the row is listed but not counted. A March 2025 progress report gives a total AiNed budget of €189 million for 2022 to 2029, which conflicts with €204.5 million. See gaps.md.

rows.title: Government-wide vision on generative AI: national AI validation team
rows.promised: Set up a national government AI validation team to assess available AI applications, alongside the vision on generative AI.
rows.notes: The page announces the team without an amount.

rows.body: Cabinet (Ministries of Economic Affairs and of Defence)
rows.title: AI factory in Groningen
rows.promised: Contribute €70 million from the Cabinet to an AI factory in Groningen, within a planned total of up to €200 million with €60 million from the region and a €70 million EU co-financing request.
rows.amount_as_stated: €70 million from the Cabinet (total up to €200 million)
rows.notes: Only the Cabinet's own €70 million is counted. The €60 million regional share is not a national government commitment, and the €70 million EU share was a pending request, which would appear in the EU AI Factory rows if granted. The proposal was submitted to EuroHPC on 27 June 2025 subject to parliamentary approval of the budget changes.

delivery.evidence_type: progress report by the announcing body
delivery.summary: A Cabinet letter to Parliament of 13 October 2025 reports that EuroHPC awarded the EU subsidy (about €71.7 million) against a total investment of about €202.6 million; the expertise centre starts in 2026 and the supercomputer is expected at full capacity in 2027.
delivery.notes: The letter gives national and regional money together (about €130.9 million), so the Cabinet's own €70 million is not separated and no amount is recorded.

flags: evidenced amount exceeds the promised amount (different bases; see the contributing rows)

rates_note: From the ECB daily history bundled in the Python package CurrencyConverter 0.18.23 (data runs 1999-01-04 to 2026-10-30). The ECB's own download and data API were not reachable from the build environment.
